FIRE HAZARD AND SAMSUNG WILL NOT HELP!!!!! - I did not purchase this from Amazon, but still wanted to give a review to possibly deter other customers who are considering this stove or ANY OTHER SAMSUNG APPLIANCE. About 2 years in, I contacted Samsung to tell them that the display was cracking and I needed them to replace. They deemed it a 'cosmetic issue' and wouldn't go further. Since I didn't know better, I didn't pursue it, until the cracking got worse and worse and the 'SAMSUNG' letters even started coming off! Ended up finding out that this was due to the extreme heat that comes up from the oven to the top of the stove. OMG!! So now I am fighting with the warranty people, because Samsung, who made this lemon, will not stand behind it. Their warranty only covered one year. I will continue to get Samsung televisions, but will be smart enough in the future to buy my appliances from manufacturers that have been in the appliance business long enough to know what they're doing. Overheating of an appliance that causes cracking is not a cosmetic issue!!

Universal Valve Great Value! - If you were like me, you searched for a replacement valve for your furnace humidifier and became confused by the large selection and wide range of prices. Don't be confused by a specific brand or the different applications that they list. As long as fittings look like the ones one your valve, this one will work for you. Every furnace valve works on standard furnace power which is universal in North America. This is a simple repair that anyone with basic wiring skills can do. the voltage involved cannot harm you. Just turn off the water valve, undo your fitting, cut your wires and remove the old valve. Splice the new wires onto the old ones (no positive or negative since it's AC), screw the new valve back into position, screw the water lines back on (follow the arrows for flow direction) and turn your water back on. You did the job for $18 and it only took about 20 minutes!!

Chemex filters are necessary for the best coffee in a Chemex pot - I've been brewing coffee for decades in a Chemex coffee pot. When my supply of the Chemex Bonded Unbleached Pre-folded Square Coffee Filters was depleting, I purchased a reusable hemp filter, thinking that a difference would not be noticeable. I was so wrong. These bonded paper filters, when moistened with water before filling with freshly ground coffee, produce a coffee that displays the coffee essence without residual solids or added bitterness from the fabric or paper. The folded square design allows the user to simply pull one free corner to turn a square into a cone that allows for perfect filtering of the hot water as it's gently poured into the coffee carafe. By slowly adding the water, you can control the drip and my preference is to pour around the outer edge instead of directly into the center of the filter. In all these years, I have never had a Chemex filter break or slip through and into the carafe, as I've had occur with the hemp filter. I also like the Chemex round filters and have just ordered a package, so I'll review those once I recall how they compare for me. I purchased a case of these pre-folded squares some time ago, so I don't remember my impression of the other filters. If you care about the taste of your coffee, then I absolutely recommend using these with your Chemex.
